deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is studying systems of pseudo-lines (pseudoline arrangements in the projective plane) and the combinatorial 'space of positions' of an additional pseudo-line D relative to a given arrangement. As far as the surrounding pages show:
- For each such D he builds a cell-like complex Delta_D.
- Its vertices are relative positions of D. Its arcs are 'specialization' arcs (D degenerates to a more special position, e.g. passing through a vertex) and their reverses, 'generalization' arcs.
- He then tries to glue ('recollements') the complexes Delta_D and Delta_D' for neighbouring D, D', e.g. related by sweeping D across a vertex ('balayage au-dessus d'un sommet').
- The transition isomorphisms are fixed by a 'parallel transport' convention.

The goal is to obtain the correct 2-dimensional cells: closed circuits of elementary moves that should bound a disc around a codimension-2 degenerate configuration. The most important of these is a 'position superposition', where D comes to coincide with, or be superposed on, another pseudo-line of the system.

The previous page lists candidate conventions for the generalization arc paired with a given specialization arc. It discards some of them because they produce intuitively 'idiotic' circuits: starting near a pseudo-line D one moves away from D instead of turning around it.

This page:
- Crossed-out start: the earlier failure is attributed to having neglected the exceptional specializations (towards superposition positions). There are two variants that allow one to specialize directly into a superposition position.
- Main text: he has verified, 'sauf erreur' (admitting he made quite a few errors during the check), which of three candidate conventions or local configurations A1, A2, B2 yield the 'good circuits' around a superposition position.
- He notes that only B2 had been handled badly, possibly 'complètement raté'. The reading is uncertain. He gives an aside that for a whole day he had for some reason been working on B2.
- He ranks A2 as most interesting, then A1. He has again tried, apparently without success, to understand the circuits A1 gives rise to.

Mathematically, this is the search for a coherent choice of 2-cells or relations, a 'flip/mutation' calculus, making the graph of positions of a pseudo-line into a simply connected (or correctly connected) 2-complex. The page is a progress report on case-checking rather than a statement of a result.
errors: No mathematical claim is stated precisely enough to check. Grothendieck himself flags the verification as error-prone ('sauf erreur', 'j'ai fait pas mal d'erreurs encore').
The crossed-out passage records an earlier error: the exceptional specializations to superposition positions had been neglected.

ideas.what: Graph/complex of relative positions of an extra pseudo-line w.r.t. a pseudoline arrangement, with specialization/generalization arcs
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of an oriented matroid (rank 3), single-element extensions; cell structure of the arrangement's complement / Salvetti-type complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler (extension spaces, 1993); Salvetti (1987)

ideas.what: Determining the correct 2-cells (circuits around codimension-2 'superposition' degenerations) via a gluing convention / parallel transport between the complexes Delta_D
ideas.modern_name: Relations of the mutation (triangle-flip) graph; Ringel homotopy theorem; higher Bruhat orders B(n,2)

ideas.what: Case analysis of candidate conventions A1, A2, B2 for good circuits around a superposition position
ideas.modern_name: local coherence checks of a 2-complex structure

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a coherent 2-cell structure, with circuits around 'superposition' degenerations, on the combinatorial space of positions of a pseudo-line relative to an arrangement. He reports partial success (A2, B2) and failure to understand the circuits of A1. This is an early independent approach to the topology of extension spaces / mutation graphs of pseudoline arrangements, predating the oriented-matroid literature of the late 1980s and 1990s. The thread is left open on this page.
missed.quote: Le plus intéressant, après A2, semble bien être A1, mais je viens encore d'essayer de comprendre les circuits auxquels il donne naissance, sans y réussir.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Topology of extension spaces of oriented matroids is still partly open: the extension-space conjecture fails in general (Mnëv–Ziegler), but questions remain in rank 3. A documented 1983-84 attempt might be of historical interest to that community. The page itself, however, contains no finished result.

deep.surprise_reason: Working notes of a case verification with no clearly stated result. They are of interest only as evidence of Grothendieck's early, independent approach to the combinatorial topology of pseudoline arrangements, a field that later developed through oriented matroids.
transcription_corrections: 'les trois positions A1, A2, B2' is more likely 'les trois possibilités A1, A2, B2'.

'il n'y a que B2 que [?] devienne complète [?] - il semblait que c'était mal' is probably 'il n'y a que B2 que j'avais complètement raté (car il semblerait que j'étais [...] sur B2 que mes [...] avaient [porté] pendant une journée, Dieu sait pourquoi!)'. The reading is uncertain.
'les circuits aux points il donne naissance, tous y réalisés' is most likely 'les circuits auxquels il donne naissance, sans y réussir'.
'j'ai fait par mal d'erreurs' should read 'j'ai fait pas mal d'erreurs'.
Crossed-out opening: 'car en revanche' is probably 'Car en fait, c'est dû en fait à ce que je n'ai pas tenu compte des cas de spécialisation exceptionnels (vers les pos. superposition)'.
